newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Barlow to invest 90 mln rand in tube unit.
newsitem.headline: Barlow to invest 90 mln rand in tube unit.

text.p: South African industrial group Barlow said on Friday its RIH unit is to invest 90 million rand in its tube manufacturing division to upgrade and modernise equipment and facilities.
The upgrade programme, which would take about 18 months, would equip the group to improve productivity, efficiencies and quality, group chairman Warren Clewlow said in a statement.
It would also enable the group to reinforce its local market dominance and exploit new international markets.
"The international market is increasing in importance to us and we now derive a quarter of our attributable earnings from this source," Clewlow said.
"The upgrade will also equip RIH to exploit new markets for products of higher specification and value-added products," he added.

RIH managing director Mike Coward said the modernisations in the tube division extended a programme begun when the group acquired the tubular interests of engineering group Dorbyl Ltd in October 1994.
He said a key aspect of the improvements would be an upgrade of employee skills and training.

The RIH group is South Africa's largest producer and distributror of welded carbon and stainless steel tube, pipe and related value added products, and holds a major share in the country's structural and conveyance pipe markets.
It also merchandises steel products nationally and, through its international trading interests, is a major exporter of steel tube.
RIH curently exports to more than 50 countries in the Middle East, Far East, America, UK and Africa.
